source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 953 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 953 was established by Ordinance No. 29979, passed by the Dallas City Council on January13, 2016. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 953 is established on property located at the western terminus of Whispering Cedars Drive. The size of PD 953 is approximately 87.39 acres. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Purpose
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.103. PURPOSE.

The purpose of this article is to protect and enhance an irreplaceable natural environment by:

(1) Allowing minimal improvements in protected large tree canopy areas.

(2) Preserving tree canopy areas adjacent to the escarpment.

(3) Restricting future expansions of a camp recreation center to designated low impact areas.

(4) Protecting existing trees in areas designated for future development.

(5) Allowing alternate paving materials to minimize impermeable surfaces.

(6) Aiding in the ecological balance of the natural environment by contributing to the processes of air purification, oxygen regeneration, and groundwater recharge.

(7) Conserving energy and water.

(8) Enhancing the beautification of the city. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) CAMP RECREATION CENTER means an area providing recreational facilities such as playgrounds; parks; game courts; camp grounds, including cabins and tents; swimming pools; private stable; patron lodging; resident, staff, and caretaker lodging; playing fields; program areas; and facilities to accommodate camping participants, including facilities for the care and maintenance of grounds, animals, structures, and machinery.

(2) EXISTING IMPROVEMENTS means a building or structure existing on the Property on January 13, 2016.

(3) FLEXIBLE BASE means crushed stone or crushed concrete meeting the requirements of the 2004 Edition of the Texas Department of Transportation, “Standard Specifications for Construction and Maintenance of Highways, Streets and Bridges,” as amended.

(4) PATRON LODGING means a lodging facility that provides room, board, and sleeping arrangements for up to 30 consecutive days to persons using a camp recreation center.

(5) RESIDENT, STAFF, AND CARETAKER LODGING means a facility that provides room and board, including dwelling units and suites, that are exclusively for members of the staff and persons assisting in the operation of a camp recreation center.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.105. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 953A: development and landscape plan. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Development And Landscape Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.106. DEVELOPMENT AND LANDSCAPE PLAN.

(a) For a camp recreation center, development and use of the Property must comply with the development and landscape plan (Exhibit 953A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development and landscape plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the A(A) Agricultural District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the A(A) Agricultural District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the A(A) Agricultural District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the A(A) Agricultural District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following additional main use is permitted by right:

-- Camp recreation center. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.108. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the A(A) Agricultural District apply.

(b) Height for a camp recreation center.

(1) Maximum height. Unless further restricted under Subparagraph (2), maximum structure height is:

(A) 110 feet for zip line towers, rock climbing walls, rappelling towers, and other similar recreational structures;

(B) 65 feet for a maximum of three observation towers; and

(C) 36 feet for all other structures.

(2) Residential proximity slope. Any portion of a structure over 26 feet in height may not be located above a residential proximity slope as defined in Section 51A-4.412. Exception: Except for chimneys, structures listed in Section 51A-4.408(a)(2) may project through the residential proximity slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height,

or a maximum height of 12 feet above the slope, whichever is less. Chimneys may project through the residential proximity slope to a maximum height 12 feet above the slope and 12 feet above the maximum structure height. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Camp recreation center.

(1) Off-street parking: 24 off-street parking spaces plus one space for each cabin or dwelling unit are required.

(2) Off-street loading: None required. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Fences
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.112. FENCES.

Fences in a required front yard may be a maximum height of eight feet. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Landscaping And Tree Replacement
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.113. LANDSCAPING AND TREE REPLACEMENT.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping and tree replacement must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Camp recreation center.

(1) In general. Landscaping must be provided as shown on the development and landscape plan. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development and landscape plan, the text of this article controls.

(2) Tree replacement. Except as provided in this paragraph, Section 51A- 10.134 applies. Protected trees may count toward replacement trees on an inch for inch basis if all the replacement trees are located on the same artificial lot and identified on the building permit application. Protected trees may only be counted once toward replacement tree requirements.

(3) Forested areas.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, forested areas shown on the development and landscape plan must remain in a natural state.

(B) Roadways, pathways, utilities, structures less than 1,000 square feet, and primitive campgrounds are permitted in forested areas.

(c) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.114. SIGNS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Detached premise signs.

(1) A maximum of three detached premise signs are allowed.

(2) Each detached premise sign may not exceed 100 square feet in effective area and 25 feet in height.

(3) Detached premise signs are allowed in a front, side, or rear yard. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Paving For A Camp Recreation Center Use
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.115. PAVING FOR A CAMP RECREATION CENTER USE.

(a) Off-street parking areas may be constructed of a 6-inch-thick section of flexible base with a Triaxial geogrid over a compacted subgrade.

(b) Fire lanes may be constructed of an 8-inch-thick section of flexible base with a Triaxial geogrid over a compacted subgrade and must meet the standards set forth in the Dallas Fire Code. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29979)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-953.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29979)
